# BKV Reports Q3 2026 Results, Cost Reimbursement Agreement with Leading Frontier AI Lab, and Verra Carbon Credit Certification


November 05, 2026 7:00 am EST[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_0cac7037cbfe0e8e4c82f9b526992140/bkvcorp/news/2026-11-05_BKV_Reports_Q3_2026_Results_Cost_Reimbursement_240.pdf)


## Related Documents


[Earnings Webcast Audio](https://viavid.webcasts.com/starthere.jsp?ei=1778306&tp_key=4001d45467)


[Presentation PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_0cac7037cbfe0e8e4c82f9b526992140/bkvcorp/db/2526/24711/presentation/BKV_2026_IR_Presentation_3Q26_Final.pdf)


DENVER--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- BKV Corporation (“BKV” or the “Company”) (NYSE: BKV) today reported financial and operational results for the third quarter of 2026, along with guidance for the fourth quarter of 2026. In addition, the Company is announcing an expanded scope for its Phase 1 modular power development in Temple, TX, supported by a Cost Reimbursement Agreement with a Leading Frontier AI Lab, and Verra carbon credit certification.


**Third Quarter 2026 Highlights**


- Net income attributable to BKV of $29.4 million or $0.27 per diluted share
- Adjusted Net Income attributable to BKV of $39.9 million or $0.36 per diluted share
- Adjusted EBITDAX attributable to BKV of $132.7 million
- Net cash provided by operating activities of $164.5 million
- Net cash provided by operating activities before working capital of $112.7 million
- Accrued capital expenditures of $77.8 million
- Adjusted Free Cash Flow before Power Growth attributable to BKV of $31.2 million
- Average net production of 981.2 MMcfe/d
- Total generation from the Power JV’s Temple plants of 2,317 GWh
- CCUS quarterly sequestration of approximately 55,200 metric tons of CO2 equivalent
- Net Leverage Ratio of 2.41x
- Completed $575.0 million Convertible Senior Notes Offering at an annual rate of 1.625%


**Cost Reimbursement Agreement with a Leading Frontier AI Lab for Modular Power Development**


BKV-BPP Power (“Power JV”) entered into a cost reimbursement agreement (“CRA”) with a Leading Frontier AI Lab supporting an increase in planned modular power generation at the Temple Energy Complex to 400 MW from 200 MW. If mutually agreeable offtake arrangements are not agreed to by November 18, 2026, the CRA covers up to approximately $179 million. The agreement contemplates an extension to December 21, 2026, and the ability to extend further, each on mutual agreement. The intended offtaker may elect to take assignment of the equipment supply contract, if not retained by the Power JV, in which case it would reimburse the Power JV for eligible costs, subject to an aggregate cap of $374.1 million. The CRA allows BKV to maintain its development schedule while advancing commercial discussions toward a long-term power purchase agreement (“PPA”).


**Equipment Supply Agreement Backed by Agreement with a Leading Investment-Grade Hyperscaler**


As previously announced in October, a wholly owned subsidiary of BKV entered into an equipment supply agreement with a Tier 1 supplier for the purchase of combined-cycle gas turbine (“CCGT”) power generation equipment for one of the Company’s prospective power generation projects in Texas representing approximately 1.2 GW. BKV also announced a backstop agreement with a leading investment-grade hyperscaler, under which the hyperscaler has agreed to reimburse a portion of BKV’s costs associated with the equipment and related project work. This investment-grade hyperscaler is also the intended offtaker for the prospective power generation project.


**Verra Carbon Credit Certification Unlocks Carbon Sequestered Gas**


BKV became the first company to receive carbon credit certification from Verra for CO₂ permanently sequestered through its CCUS operations. This milestone enables the Company to monetize carbon credits through its Carbon Sequestered Gas (“CSG”), a first-of-its-kind, third-party-verified carbon-neutral natural gas product. With verification complete, BKV can begin delivering CSG under its previously announced arrangements with Kiewit and Gunvor, while pursuing additional opportunities to market CSG to customers seeking reliable, lower-carbon energy solutions.


**Strategic Barnett Shale Acquisition Highlights**


As previously announced, on September 15, 2026, BKV completed the acquisition of upstream, midstream and carbon capture and sequestration (“CCS”) assets in the Barnett Shale, further strengthening its position as one of the basin’s leading operators. The acquisition added approximately 65 MMcfe/d of production (more than 50% liquids) and approximately 0.35 Tcfe of proved developed producing reserves. The acquired assets also include a cryogenic natural gas processing plant with 180 MMcf/d of capacity, approximately 340 miles of owned natural gas gathering infrastructure, 225 miles of owned water gathering infrastructure and two saltwater disposal wells. Additionally, the acquisition included an operating CCS facility that sequestered greater than 100,000 metric tons of CO₂ during the twelve months ended September 30, 2026.


“Our upstream business delivered another strong quarter, with continued operational outperformance providing a solid foundation as we advanced our strategic growth initiatives,” said Chris Kalnin, Chief Executive Officer of BKV. “We also made meaningful commercial progress in our power business, securing a cost reimbursement agreement for modular generation equipment and a previously announced backstop agreement with an investment-grade hyperscaler supporting our CCGT equipment commitments.”


“These milestones reflect our deliberate, disciplined approach to developing additional power generation capacity,” continued Kalnin. “We are encouraged by the progress of our commercial discussions and remain focused on securing long-term power purchase agreements that support our growth objectives. Combined with continued execution across our upstream and carbon capture businesses, we believe this progress positions BKV to advance its closed-loop strategy and create sustainable, long-term shareholder value.”

“Our strong upstream cash flow, disciplined capital commitments and recent capital markets transactions have further strengthened our financial position and provided substantial liquidity to support our strategic growth initiatives,” said David Tameron, Chief Financial Officer of BKV. “As we advance our phased power development strategy, we remain focused on preserving financial flexibility and maintaining a strong balance sheet.”


“The announced cost reimbursement agreement for modular generation equipment and the previously disclosed hyperscaler backstop for combined-cycle equipment reflect our disciplined approach to structuring capital commitments,” continued Tameron. “These arrangements provide important financial protections and flexibility as we advance commercial discussions, positioning us to pursue significant growth opportunities while prudently managing capital exposure and development risk.”

**Segment Operational Results - Third Quarter 2026**


**Power Segment**


BKV has made tangible commercial progress toward securing long-term PPAs across its power development platform. The Company announced an equipment supply agreement for approximately 1.2 GW of CCGT capacity, supported by a backstop agreement with an investment-grade hyperscaler. The Power JV also entered into a cost reimbursement agreement with a leading Frontier AI Lab, supporting an increase in planned modular generation at the Temple Energy Complex to 400 MW from 200 MW. These agreements represent important commercial milestones as BKV advances discussions toward long-term PPAs. With the additional modular generation equipment, the Company's existing and planned power generation assets now represent approximately 3.3 GW of potential capacity.


The Temple I and II facilities continued to demonstrate strong operational reliability during the quarter, achieving a combined capacity factor of 71.7% and total generation of 2,317 GWh. Plant availability remained high with an average equivalent availability factor of 96% reflecting continued operational execution across both facilities.


Despite record power demand across ERCOT during the quarter, wholesale power prices and spark spreads were below expectations, as increased renewable generation and battery storage moderated peak pricing. BKV remains confident in the long-term fundamentals of the ERCOT market, supported by a substantial backlog of large-load interconnection requests and anticipated demand growth.

**Upstream-Midstream Segment**


BKV’s Upstream-Midstream business had another strong quarter of operational performance. Production came in above the high end of the guidance range, excluding the contribution from the Barnett acquisition completed during the quarter, while development capital expenditures came in below the low end of the guided range. The production outperformance was primarily driven by continued new well development outperformance and peer-leading base decline management. Additionally, the Barnett acquisition completed on September 15, 2026, provided an incremental production contribution during the quarter. The Upstream-Midstream business continues to outperform on multiple levels and generate strong cash flow, while continued improvements in capital efficiency support disciplined investment across the Company’s broader platform.


The Company completed its first full quarter of internally marketing all of its natural gas production. Bringing marketing in-house expands BKV’s closed-loop strategy and creates potential margin opportunities through retention of previously outsourced marketing economics, optimization of delivery points, transportation and basis, enhanced commercial execution and, over time, power-linked optimization and decarbonization monetization levers.

**Carbon Capture Utilization and Sequestration (“CCUS”)**


During the third quarter, BKV expanded its operational CCUS portfolio to four projects following the acquisition of an additional injection facility as part of its upstream Barnett acquisition. Together, these projects represent an annual CO₂ sequestration run rate of approximately 350,000 metric tons. Since commencing initial injection at Barnett Zero in November 2023, BKV has significantly expanded its operating footprint and sequestration capacity in less than three years.


Total injection volumes for the third quarter were 55,200 metric tons of CO₂, including 15 days of injection volumes of 5,400 metric tons from the acquired CCS injection well.


The Company remains focused on developing its broader CCUS pipeline in collaboration with its joint venture partner, CIP, and working closely with the State of Louisiana on its Class VI permit applications. The Company remains on track to achieve its targeted annual injection run rate of 1.5 million metric tons in 2028.


**Liquidity and Debt**


As of September 30, 2026, BKV had cash and cash equivalents of $619.6 million and restricted cash of $16.3 million related to the Power segment Temple Term Loan Facility. Total principal debt as of September 30, 2026 was $2.0 billion, with total net debt of $1.4 billion. Total principal debt was made up of the 2031 Convertible Senior Notes of $575.0 million, the 2030 Senior Notes of $500.0 million, an RBL balance of $240.0 million, the Promissory Note of $46.0 million, and Power segment debt of $676.7 million. Power segment debt included $162.0 million of borrowings under the Temple I Loan Agreements, $370.3 million of borrowings under the Temple Term Loan Facility, Power Equipment Financing Facility of $84.4 million, and a Temple Revolving Facility balance of $60.0 million.


During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, BKV’s JV partners contributed an aggregate $78.8 million, comprised of $65.4 million from Banpu Power US Corporation (“BPPUS”) and $13.4 million from CIP. BKV expects continued contributions through year end.


As of September 30, 2026, total liquidity for BKV was $1.2 billion, which consisted of $619.6 million in cash and cash equivalents and $544.5 million available capacity under the Company’s RBL. RBL availability as of September 30, 2026, was based on the elected commitment amount of $800.0 million, less an outstanding balance of $240.0 million and $15.5 million of letters of credit.

**About BKV Corporation**


Headquartered in Denver, Colorado, BKV Corporation is a forward-thinking, growth-driven energy company focused on creating value for its stockholders. BKV's core business is to produce natural gas from its owned and operated upstream assets. BKV’s overall business is organized into four business lines: natural gas production; natural gas gathering, processing and transportation; power generation; and carbon capture, utilization and sequestration. BKV (and its predecessor entity) was founded in 2015, and BKV and its employees are committed to building a different kind of energy company. BKV is one of the top 15 gas-weighted natural gas producers in the United States and the largest natural gas producer by gross operated volume in the Barnett Shale. BKV Corporation is the parent company for the BKV family of companies. For more information, visit the BKV website at[www.bkv.com](http://www.bkv.com/) .

**Supplemental Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


This release includes the non-GAAP financial measures described below. These non-GAAP measures are intended to provide additional information only and should not be considered as alternatives to, or more meaningful than, net income (loss) attributable to BKV, basic and diluted EPS, net income (loss), net cash provided by operating activities, or any other measure calculated in accordance with GAAP.


As a result of the Company’s acquisition of an additional 25% ownership interest in and consolidation of the Power JV as of January 30, 2026, the Company changed the presentation of its non-GAAP measures of Combined Adjusted EBITDAX, Adjusted Free Cash Flow, and Adjusted Free Cash Flow Margin beginning in the first quarter of 2026. The Company now discloses Adjusted Net Income (Loss) attributable to BKV, Adjusted EPS attributable to BKV, Adjusted EBITDAX, Adjusted EBITDAX attributable to BKV, Adjusted EBITDAX attributable to Noncontrolling Interests, Adjusted Free Cash Flow before Power Growth, and Adjusted Free Cash Flow before Power Growth attributable to BKV. Such non-GAAP measures have been presented in this release for the comparative period and have been calculated based on the definitions below.


***Net Leverage Ratio***


The Company defines Net Leverage Ratio as total debt less cash and cash equivalents, and restricted cash, divided by Adjusted EBITDAX for the most recent quarter’s annualized Adjusted EBITDAX (the quarter’s Adjusted EBITDAX multiplied by four). The Company uses this metric to evaluate the total carrying value of debt relative to the Company’s ability to generate cash through Adjusted EBITDAX. This metric also provides management with a benchmark of debt levels while considering growth opportunities and the Company’s ability to manage periods of commodity price volatility. ​

***Adjusted Net Income (Loss) Attributable to BKV and Adjusted EPS Attributable to BKV***


The Company defines Adjusted Net Income (Loss) attributable to BKV as net income (loss) attributable to BKV before (i) net unrealized derivative (gains) losses, (ii) forward month gas settlements, (iii) impairment of assets held for sale, (iv) other nonrecurring transactions, and (v) the tax impact of these adjustments calculated using a 23% statutory rate. The Company defines Adjusted EPS attributable to BKV as Adjusted Net Income (Loss) attributable to BKV divided by diluted weighted average common shares outstanding.


The Company believes Adjusted Net Income (Loss) attributable to BKV and Adjusted EPS attributable to BKV are useful performance measures because they allow the Company to effectively evaluate its operating performance and results of operations from period to period and against its peers, without regard to financing methods, corporate form, capital structure, or one-time events. The Company excludes the items listed above from net income (loss) attributable to BKV in arriving at Adjusted Net Income (Loss) attributable to BKV and Adjusted EPS attributable to BKV because these amounts can vary substantially from company to company within the industry depending upon accounting methods and book values of assets, capital structures, and the method by which the assets were acquired. The Company's presentation of Adjusted Net Income (Loss) attributable to BKV and Adjusted EPS attributable to BKV should not be construed as an inference that its results will be unaffected by unusual or non-recurring items. Other companies, including other companies in the industry, may not use Adjusted Net Income (Loss) attributable to BKV and Adjusted EPS attributable to BKV or may calculate these measures differently than as presented in this release, limiting their usefulness as comparative measures.

***Adjusted EBITDAX, Adjusted EBITDAX Attributable to BKV, and Adjusted EBITDAX Attributable to Noncontrolling Interests***


The Company defines Adjusted EBITDAX as net income (loss) before (i) depreciation, depletion, amortization, and accretion, (ii) exploration and impairment expense, (iii) net unrealized gains (losses) on derivatives, (iv) net interest expense, (v) interest expense, related parties, (vi) equity-based compensation expense, (vii) income tax benefit (expense), and (viii) other nonrecurring transactions. Adjusted EBITDAX attributable to BKV is defined as Adjusted EBITDAX less Adjusted EBITDAX attributable to Noncontrolling Interests.


The Company excludes the items listed above from net income (loss) in arriving at Adjusted EBITDAX because these amounts can vary substantially from company to company within the industry depending upon accounting methods and book values of assets, capital structures, and the method by which the assets were acquired. Adjusted EBITDAX should not be considered an alternative to, or more meaningful than, net income (loss) determined in accordance with GAAP. Certain items excluded from Adjusted EBITDAX are significant components in understanding and assessing a company’s financial performance, such as a company’s cost of capital and tax burden, as well as the historic costs of depreciable assets, none of which are reflected in Adjusted EBITDAX. The Company’s presentation of Adjusted EBITDAX should not be construed as an inference that its results will be unaffected by unusual or non-recurring items. Other companies, including other companies in the industry, may not use Adjusted EBITDAX or may calculate this measure differently than as presented in this release, limiting its usefulness as a comparative measure.


Adjusted EBITDAX is a supplemental non-GAAP financial measure that is used by the Company’s management and external users of its consolidated financial statements, such as industry analysts, investors, lenders, rating agencies, and others to more effectively evaluate the Company’s operating performance and results of operations from period to period and against industry peers. The Company believes Adjusted EBITDAX is a useful performance measure because it allows the Company to effectively evaluate its operating performance and results of operations from period to period and against industry peers, without regard to its financing methods, corporate form, or capital structure.

***Adjusted Free Cash Flow before Power Growth and Adjusted Free Cash Flow before Power Growth Attributable to BKV***


The Company defines Adjusted Free Cash Flow before Power Growth as net cash provided by operating activities, excluding cash paid for contingent consideration and changes in operating assets and liabilities, less total cash paid for capital expenditures (excluding leasehold costs and acquisitions), excluding strategic power growth capital expenditures. Adjusted Free Cash Flow before Power Growth attributable to BKV is defined as Adjusted Free Cash Flow before Power Growth, less Adjusted EBITDAX attributable to Noncontrolling Interests, with net interest expense attributable to noncontrolling interests added back, plus net contributions from CCUS noncontrolling interests.


Adjusted Free Cash Flow before Power Growth and Adjusted Free Cash Flow before Power Growth attributable to BKV are not measures of net cash provided by or used in operating activities as determined in accordance with GAAP. These measures are supplemental non-GAAP financial measures used by management and external users of the Company's financial statements, including industry analysts, investors, lenders and rating agencies, to assess the Company's ability to internally fund its capital program, service or incur additional debt and pay dividends. Adjusted Free Cash Flow before Power Growth reflects cash flow available to fund the Company's capital program, excluding strategic power growth capital expenditures, while Adjusted Free Cash Flow before Power Growth attributable to BKV further adjusts for noncontrolling interests to reflect amounts attributable to the Company's common shareholders. The Company believes these measures are useful indicators of liquidity because they facilitate period-over-period comparisons of cash flow provided by operating activities and the Company's ability to internally fund its capital program (including acquisitions), reduce leverage, fund acquisitions and return capital to shareholders. Adjusted Free Cash Flow before Power Growth and Adjusted Free Cash Flow before Power Growth attributable to BKV should not be considered alternatives to, or more meaningful than, net income (loss) or net cash provided by (used in) operating activities determined in accordance with GAAP. Other companies, including other companies in the industry, may define these measures differently, limiting their usefulness as comparative measures.
